Format & marks

Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section requires a written programme with programme notes on every piece totalling 1,200-1,600 words (musical and historical context, structure and form, significant musical elements; sources must be credited and not plagiarised). The balance and order of the programme are also judged. No viva or quick study.
